content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review. No code or implementation plan has been created yet.

Scope includes:

- Private personal bookmark libraries
- Add, edit, open, and permanently delete bookmarks
- Titles, descriptions, tags, and collections
- Search, filtering, and sorting
- URL validation, normalization, and duplicate detection
- Responsive web application
- Explicit exclusions such as sharing, browser extensions, import/export, and automatic metadata retrieval

Artifacts:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Checklist: all 16 quality checks passed

The `speckit-specify` skill shaped the user stories, testable requirements, edge cases, assumptions, and measurable outcomes.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll proceed to the implementation-plan gate.

Thanks for putting this together — I read through it, and a lot of it matches what I have in my head. Saving a link, editing it, tags, search, filtering, sorting, catching duplicates, and being careful before permanently deleting something — that's all the right idea.

But a few things I really expect are either missing or excluded, and I'd want them sorted before I sign off on this as the plan:

1. **Filling in details automatically.** This is a big one for me. When I paste in a link, I expect the app to go grab the page's title, a short description, the little site icon, and ideally a preview picture on its own, so I'm not typing all of that by hand every single time. I saw the spec specifically says that's *out* of scope — that won't work for me. Some of the tedium of saving a bookmark is exactly what I'm trying to avoid.

2. **A "read it later" pile.** I often save things I haven't read yet. I'd want to mark a bookmark as unread, see just my unread ones on their own, and then mark it read so it drops off that list.

3. **Setting things aside without deleting.** Right now the only way to get something out of my main list is to permanently delete it. I'd want a way to tuck a bookmark away — hide it from my normal list and searches but keep it — and be able to look at those set-aside ones separately and bring them back. Delete-for-good should be the separate, final option.

4. **Smarter searching.** Plain word search is good, but I'd also expect to search by a tag directly, to search an exact phrase in quotes, and to combine things (this tag but not that one, this or that). And when I'm typing a tag onto a bookmark, I'd like it to suggest tags I already use.

5. **Personal notes.** Beyond a short description, I'd like to jot my own longer notes on a bookmark and have them show nicely when I look at it. And my search should look inside those notes too.

6. **Doing things in bulk.** When I've got a lot selected — or everything matching what I'm currently looking at — I'd want to tag them, mark them read, set them aside, or delete them all in one go.

7. **Saving a search I use a lot.** If I've got a search-plus-tags combination I keep coming back to, I'd like to save that as its own named view to jump to later.

A couple of these (like import/export) I'm honestly fine leaving out for now, so I won't push on those. But the automatic detail-fetching, read-later, set-aside-vs-delete, richer search, notes, and bulk actions are things I'd genuinely use. Could you fold those in and show me the revised version?

content:
The revised specification now includes all seven requested capabilities as first-release requirements:

- Automatic title, description, site icon, and preview-image retrieval
- An unread/read-later queue
- Reversible archiving, separate from permanent deletion
- Advanced search with tags, quoted phrases, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and grouping
- Existing-tag suggestions
- Longer searchable notes with readable formatting
- Bulk tagging, read-state changes, archiving, restoring, and deletion
- Named saved views based on live search and filter criteria

Important defaults are explicit:

- New bookmarks start unread unless changed.
- Opening a bookmark does not automatically mark it read.
- Metadata failure never prevents manual saving.
- Metadata is captured when saving rather than refreshed continuously.
- Archived bookmarks are excluded from the main library, normal searches, and unread queue.
- Bulk “all matches” actions include results beyond the current page and show the exact affected count.
- Permanent deletion remains distinct from archiving and requires confirmation.

Review the full revised artifact here:

- [Revised bookmark manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Updated quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

The revised draft contains 8 prioritized user stories, 49 functional requirements, and 12 measurable outcomes. All 16 quality checks pass with no unresolved clarification markers.

The `speckit-specify` workflow kept these changes in the specification and expanded the relevant acceptance scenarios, edge cases, entities, assumptions, and success measures. No planning or implementation has started.

Please approve this revision or flag anything else you want changed.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I asked about, and reading through it, it matches what I pictured. The automatic detail-fetching with a graceful fallback when it can't get them, the unread/read-later queue with sensible defaults, archiving as a reversible "set aside" that's clearly separate from deleting for good, the richer searching by tag and exact phrase and the and/or/not combinations, tag suggestions while I type, longer notes that are searchable, bulk actions with a clear count of what I'm about to affect, and saved views — that's all the right idea.

I especially like the little details you called out: opening a link not marking it read on its own, a failed detail-fetch never blocking me from just saving, and the app always telling me exactly how many things a bulk action or deletion will hit before I commit. Those are exactly the kinds of things I'd worry about.

I'm happy with this as the plan. You can go ahead to the next step.

One small thing to just keep in the back of your mind for later, not a change to this — down the road I might want the app to keep its own saved copy of a page in case the original ever disappears. I don't need it now, so don't add it; I just want to flag it so it's not a surprise later.

Approved — go ahead.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review. No tasks or application code have been generated yet.

Key decisions:

- React SPA with a same-origin Fastify API
- Node.js 24 and TypeScript
- SQLite with FTS5 full-text search
- Custom parser for phrases, tags, Boolean operators, and parentheses
- SSRF-resistant metadata retrieval with DNS and redirect validation
- Searchable, safely rendered Markdown notes
- Revision-bound bulk previews so confirmed counts cannot silently change
- Encrypted cookie sessions and strict per-user data isolation
- One production process listening on `0.0.0.0:4000`
- Full-page snapshots explicitly deferred; only bounded preview-image caching is planned

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [OpenAPI contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

The API contract passes OpenAPI validation without warnings. The `speckit-plan` workflow shaped the research, architecture, data model, API boundaries, and validation strategy.

Please approve the plan or request changes. After approval, the next gate is generating the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

I'll be honest — most of this is over my head, the technical bits about how it's built aren't really something I can judge. That's your call to make.

What I do care about is that everything we agreed on is still in there, and from what I can tell it is. I noticed you've got the auto-fetching of page details being careful about not poking at private stuff, the searching by tag and phrases and the and/or/not, the notes showing up nicely and safely, the bulk actions where the count I confirm can't quietly change out from under me, and each person's bookmarks kept private to them. That all lines up with what I wanted.

I also see you've flagged the "keep its own copy of a page" idea as set aside for later, with just some preview-image caching for now — that's exactly right, that's what I asked.

Go ahead with the plan.

content:
The bookmark manager is built and running at:

**http://maker:4000/**

Review credentials:

- Email: `review@example.test`
- Password: `bookmark-review`

It includes all eight agreed areas: rich bookmark capture, advanced search, read-later, tags/collections and notes, archive/restore, bulk actions with fixed confirmation counts, saved views, and editing/permanent deletion.

Validation passed:

- 13 unit/component tests
- 5 API integration tests
- 2 desktop/mobile browser journeys
- Type checking, linting, production build, and dependency audit
- 10,000-bookmark search benchmark: 9.21 ms p95
- Live health check

The Spec Kit implementation workflow guided the build and all 94 tasks are recorded complete in [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md). Validation details are in [validation-results.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/validation-results.md).

Full offline page copies remain deliberately excluded, as agreed.

I went in and tried it myself, and it does what we agreed on. A few things I checked directly and was glad to see:

- When I saved a link without the "https" part and with odd capitalization and a trailing slash, it tidied it up into a proper address on its own.
- When I tried to save that same link again — even typed differently — it caught it and told me it's *already saved* and pointed me to the existing one, instead of making a duplicate. That's exactly the behavior I wanted.
- Marking something read worked, and setting a bookmark aside pulled it out of my main list while keeping it findable in the set-aside area — and it wasn't deleted.
- When I typed a broken search on purpose, it didn't just fail silently — it told me plainly "add a term after OR" and kept what I'd typed.
- Everything's behind a login and tied to my account.

That, plus the read-later queue, tags and notes, bulk actions with a fixed count, and saved views all being present, covers everything we talked through. The screenshot that came with it only showed the sign-in page with a note that it couldn't confirm things were working, but when I actually used the running app myself it was clearly working fine — so that was just a snapshot hiccup, not a real problem.

I'm happy with it. This is what I asked for — thank you. I'll still keep that "app keeps its own copy of a page" idea on the list for a future round, but it's not part of this and doesn't hold anything up.

Accepted.
